description: Salt March, Gandhi-Irwin Pact, Quit India, Round Table Conferences, partition role, assassination

questions.stem: The DANDI MARCH (Salt Satyagraha) was launched by Gandhi on:

options.option_text: 12 March 1930, from Sabarmati Ashram to Dandi
8 August 1942, from Bombay's Gowalia Tank Maidan
6 April 1919, from Champaran district of Bihar
30 January 1948, from Birla House at Delhi

questions.explanation: Dandi March (Salt Satyagraha) — 12 March to 6 April 1930. Gandhi + 78 followers walked ~390 km from Sabarmati Ashram (Ahmedabad) to Dandi (Gujarat coast). On 6 April, picked up natural sea-salt → broke the Salt Law. Sparked nationwide Civil Disobedience Movement. Distractor 2 = Quit India launch (Aug 1942). Distractor 3 = Champaran Satyagraha (1917). Distractor 4 = Gandhi's assassination at Birla House.

questions.stem: The QUIT INDIA MOVEMENT was launched by the AICC at Bombay on:

options.option_text: 26 January 1930, with the call for Purna Swaraj
8 August 1942, with Gandhi's 'Do or Die' call
30 December 1929, at the Lahore Congress session
9 December 1946, at the Constituent Assembly opening

questions.explanation: Quit India — 8 August 1942 at AICC session at Gowalia Tank Maidan (now August Kranti Maidan), Bombay. Gandhi gave the famous 'DO OR DIE' speech. By 9 August all major leaders arrested → leaderless mass movement (Aruna Asaf Ali hoisted flag, JP Narayan took underground role). Government cracked down hard. Marked Britain's loss of moral legitimacy in India. Distractor 1 = Independence Day (Purna Swaraj declaration). Distractor 3 = Lahore session. Distractor 4 = Constituent Assembly.

questions.stem: Mahatma Gandhi participated in the SECOND ROUND TABLE CONFERENCE held in:

options.option_text: Lahore in 1929 with the Punjabi national leaders
London in 1931 as the sole Congress representative
Karachi in 1931 alongside Subhash Chandra Bose
Calcutta in 1928 at the All-Parties conference

questions.explanation: Three Round Table Conferences in LONDON: First (1930) — boycotted by Congress. SECOND (Sep-Dec 1931) — Gandhi attended as the SOLE Congress representative after the Gandhi-Irwin Pact. Third (1932) — Congress again boycotted. Gandhi's London visit famous for his austerity, dhoti, meeting King George V, mill workers in Lancashire. Returned to India to find Congress leaders re-arrested. Distractor 1 = Lahore Congress session 1929 (Purna Swaraj). Distractor 4 = Nehru Report 1928.

questions.stem: The GANDHI-IRWIN PACT was signed in March 1931. Its key provision was:

options.option_text: Immediate independence of India from British rule
Suspension of Civil Disobedience and prisoner release
Acceptance of partition along religious-majority lines
Transfer of all Indian princely states to British Crown

questions.explanation: Gandhi-Irwin Pact (5 March 1931) — between Gandhi and Viceroy Lord Irwin. Provisions: (1) Congress to suspend Civil Disobedience Movement; (2) Government to release political prisoners (except those convicted of violent crimes); (3) Congress to attend Round Table Conference; (4) right to make salt for personal consumption restored on the coast. Critics: didn't address Bhagat Singh's death sentence (executed 23 March 1931). Distractor 1 = no, independence came in 1947. Distractor 3 = no agreement on partition then. Distractor 4 = no.

questions.stem: Gandhi's ASSASSIN was Nathuram Godse on the date:

options.option_text: 30 January 1948, while at Birla House Delhi
15 August 1947, the day of Indian independence
26 January 1950, the day of Republic Day declaration
30 January 1949, a year after partition violence

questions.explanation: Gandhi assassinated on 30 January 1948 (Friday, ~5:17 pm) at Birla House (now Gandhi Smriti), New Delhi, while walking to the prayer ground. Shot 3 times by NATHURAM GODSE (former RSS member, then with Hindu Mahasabha). Godse believed Gandhi was too pro-Muslim. Tried with Narayan Apte; both hanged 15 November 1949 at Ambala Jail. 30 January is observed as MARTYRS' DAY (Shaheed Diwas) in India. Distractor 2 = independence day (Gandhi was alive then but absent from Delhi celebrations). Distractor 3 = Republic Day. Distractor 4 = wrong year.

questions.stem: Gandhi's INDIVIDUAL SATYAGRAHA campaign of 1940-41 was led at the start by:

options.option_text: Jawaharlal Nehru, the future first PM of India
Vinoba Bhave, the noted Sarvodaya leader
Sardar Patel, the home minister of free India
Subhash Bose, leader of the INA later

questions.explanation: Individual Satyagraha — launched October 1940 by Gandhi to protest Britain's refusal to grant India self-rule despite Indian war contribution. STRATEGY — selected individuals to break specific anti-war laws and court arrest. FIRST satyagrahi: VINOBA BHAVE (later founder of Bhoodan Movement, 1951); second: Jawaharlal Nehru. Aim: limit confrontation while still asserting moral protest. ~25,000 arrested by mid-1941. Distractor 3 — Patel's role was elsewhere. Distractor 4 — Bose left Congress in 1939.

questions.stem: Gandhi's only book commonly considered his AUTOBIOGRAPHY is titled:

options.option_text: Hind Swaraj, written aboard ship in 1909
The Story of My Experiments with Truth (1929)
Discovery of India, written in 1944 by him
Glimpses of World History, by Gandhi to his daughter

questions.explanation: 'The Story of My Experiments with Truth' (Satya Na Prayogo athva Atmakatha) — Gandhi's autobiography. Originally serialised in Gujarati 'Navjivan' (1925-29). Covers his life till ~1920. Hind Swaraj (1909) — political tract written during his return voyage from London. Distractor 3 = Nehru's 'Discovery of India' (written in Ahmednagar Fort prison, 1942-44). Distractor 4 = Nehru's letters from prison to daughter Indira ('Glimpses of World History', 1934).
